subject: Mid-cycle OKR steer: capacity moves, canary rollouts, and delegation
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle OKR steer: capacity moves, canary rollouts, and delegation

Team —

We're at the halfway mark and I want to lock a compact plan for the next six weeks to keep OKR delivery on track without burning runway. Short summary of where we are: one major re-scope (embedding infra), one medium risk (latency regressions on long sequences), and a handful of smaller product scope shifts.

Concrete asks:
- Resource transfer: Laura, can you move two FE engs (1.0 FTE total) from the Console backlog to the QBR integrations squad for 6 weeks starting Oct 18? Details in the capacity-matrix.xlsx attached.
- Canary rollouts: Karthik, we need a safe canary window for the new batching changes. Aim for a 72-hour canary with automatic rollback on >1.5x p50 latency or >0.5% error spike. Draft canary-plan.md attached — please validate infra constraints.
- Escalation path: Vanessa, markus — I want a named fallback if the new quantized model introduces quality drift during canary. Proposal: immediate rollback + emergency A/B to the last verified variant; if regression persists, open a customer advisory.

Decision deadline: EOD Oct 12. If we can't land the resource move by Oct 15, we'll pivot to a reduced-scope canary (no new plugins in canary).

Attachments: QBR_playbook_v2.pdf, capacity-matrix.xlsx, canary-plan.md

Thanks — quick replies appreciated.

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
VP, Product & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle OKR steer: capacity moves, canary rollouts, and delegation

Sergio —

Thanks for the clear ask. I can free up two frontend engineers from the Console backlog, but I need to surface the downstream impact: three customer minor-scope tickets will be delayed by ~2 weeks. I'll update the roadmap note and notify CS.

If you want the transfer approved today, I'll reassign Sally M. and Omar R. to the QBR integrations squad (sprint assignment change goes live Oct 18). If we later need more capacity, I can pull one mobile PM to help with prioritization.

On the canary: agree with 72 hours. Karthik — can you confirm we have a canary cluster with metric hooks (p50/p95, error rate, token throughput) and automatic rollback? If not, we should limit the canary to internal traffic only.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle OKR steer: capacity moves, canary rollouts, and delegation

Sergio / Laura —

We have a canary cluster available but it's currently shared with a nightly ingestion job that increases memory pressure between 02:00–04:00 UTC. Two notes:
1) We should schedule the 72-hour window to avoid that ingestion window (start no earlier than 10:00 UTC).
2) The current routing stack doesn't support token-level tracing for quantized variants; we'll need a 3-hour instrumenting window before canary start. I'll open SUP-1234 and tag ops.

I'll also validate the proposed rollback criteria against p50/p95 percentiles (we typically use p95 as a stronger signal). If you want aggressive sensitivity, suggest: rollback on p95 >1.4x baseline OR error increase >0.4%.

Attachment: canary-plan.md (annotated)

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Mid-cycle OKR steer: capacity moves, canary rollouts, and delegation

Sergio/Laura —

Quick heads-up from the Acme integration side: our engineering lead is worried that a canary rollback could temporarily flip embeddings to the prior model and that will change similarity scores in active experiments. We need a migration plan for experiment continuity — can we get an advisory that outlines expected score drift windows and rollback notification cadence?

If helpful, Emma and I can join a 30-minute sync with Karthik and CS to align on the notification templates.

—Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
StratusAI

To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen@stratusai.com>

Subject: Re: Mid-cycle OKR steer: capacity moves, canary rollouts, and delegation

Thanks all — quick readout and decisions captured below so we have a clear record for the QBR: 

Decisions (as of 2026-10-12):
- Resource transfer approved: Laura to reassign Sally M. and Omar R. to QBR integrations (sprint change effective Oct 18). Laura will notify CS and update the roadmap.
- Canary window: 72 hours starting Oct 19 10:00 UTC. Karthik to open SUP-1234 for tracing work; instrumenting block scheduled Oct 18 07:00–10:00 UTC.
- Rollback criteria refined: rollback on p95 >1.4x baseline OR error rate increase >0.4%.
- External notification: Ellen/Emma — we will supply an advisory doc outlining expected embedding drift windows and notification cadence. CS will prepare templates.

Action owners & deadlines:
- Laura B.: run resource reassignment and update roadmap (due Oct 15).
- Karthik I.: SUP-1234 opened and tracing in place (due Oct 18).
- Vanessa O. & Markus K.: define fallback customer advisory language and signoff (draft due Oct 17).
- Sergio: finalize QBR talking points and attach the final canary plan to the QBR_playbook (due Oct 16).

I've attached the updated QBR_playbook_v2.pdf with an exec slide and the capacity-matrix.xlsx. I'll push the final canary-plan.md to the drive link and share after Karthik's annotations.

If there are no objections by EOD Oct 13 I'll include this plan in the leadership readout.

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
VP, Product & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
